data.long_meaning: From the Greek 'amatros', meaning 'dear' or 'beloved'. This name was borne by St. Amatruda, a seventh-century Italian saint. The name Amatruda carries the meaning “Beloved, dear one” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Amatruda usually hope their child will grow to embody beloved, dear one and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Amatruda belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Beloved, dear one.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Amatruda total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.
data.cultural_impact: The name "Amatruda" could be appreciated for its distinguished Greek origin and its historical ties to the Italian saint of the same name. It could evoke feelings of warmth, love, and affection due to the meaning 'dear' or 'beloved'. In various different cultures, it is common to give names with endearing meanings to children, allowing them to feel cherished and valued since their early years. A name like "Amatruda" could contribute to creating an atmosphere of love and care, not only within a family but also in the wider community.
data.spiritual_significance: "Amatruda" is a name rich in spiritual significance, as it is associated with St. Amatruda, an early Christian saint from the Abbey of Sancta Maria Tre cognate in Italy. Believers in the Christian faith are drawn to this name for its underlying connection to the virtue of love, an essential cornerstone of their spiritual life. St. Amatruda may be invoked as a protector and intercessor, reminding us of the power of love and the importance of caring for others in our daily lives. It may also serve as an inspiration to love our neighbors as ourselves and extend God's love to those around us.
